mainTopic: Eating before a fast that touches שבת: when תשעה באב falls next to שבת, how much may one eat beforehand, and must one finish the fast on ערב שבת?
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about eating before a fast that touches שבת. When ערב תשעה באב is on שבת, one may eat a full feast. When תשעה באב itself falls on ערב שבת, the first opinion says one eats a כביצה so as not to enter שבת fasting, and ר' עקיבא did this to show his students. ר' יוסי disagrees and says one fasts until night. The חכמים answer his argument: leaving שבת hungry after eating all day is not the same as entering שבת after fasting all day. עולא rules like ר' יוסי. The גמרא challenges this ruling from רבן גמליאל's view, which was the fixed הלכה in his day. It answers that each generation followed its own leader, and then debates a family story about a postponed תשעה באב. Finally אביי reminds רב יוסף of the source for the ruling, and the גמרא begins to question whether that source really covers ערב שבת. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A full meal is allowed when the day before the fast is שבת
steps.stepSummary: If ערב תשעה באב falls on שבת, there are no limits on eating. One may even serve a feast like שלמה המלך's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, if the day before תשעה באב falls on שבת, a person eats and drinks as much as he needs. He may put on his table even a meal like שלמה המלך's feast in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of rules about the meal before a fast. It teaches that when ערב תשעה באב is שבת, the usual limits on the last meal do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the last meal before תשעה באב (the סעודה המפסקת) is kept simple, as a sign of mourning. But on שבת we may not show mourning, so the honor of שבת wins out. That is why even a royal feast is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before the fast of תשעה באב
שלמה המלך's feast, a picture of the grandest meal possible

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a theme for the whole passage: כבוד שבת can override the usual rules of fasting and mourning.

phrases.english: And so too, the eve of the Ninth of Av
that happens to fall on Shabbat
he eats and drinks all that he needs
and he may bring up onto his table
even a meal like Solomon's feast in his time

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of fast-related rules on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ערב תשעה באב is שבת, one eats without limit, even a royal feast.

steps.title: When תשעה באב falls on Friday, one eats an egg-sized amount
steps.stepSummary: If תשעה באב itself falls on ערב שבת, one is given a כביצה of food to eat, so that he does not enter שבת while fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If תשעה באב falls on ערב שבת, they bring him an egg's volume of food and he eats it. This is so that he does not come into שבת while he is suffering from the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite situation: now the fast day itself is right before שבת. It rules that one breaks the fast with a small amount before שבת begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is not hunger as such. The concern is entering שבת in a state of עינוי (affliction), which clashes with the joy of שבת. A small amount, a כביצה, is enough to remove that state. One does not eat a full meal.

keyTerms.meaning: The volume of an egg, a small measure of food
In a state of affliction, i.e., fasting

steps.confusionAlert: The text says 'עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת' here, but this is not the same as the previous line. Before, the day BEFORE the fast was שבת. Here the FAST DAY itself is Friday.

phrases.aramaic: חָל לִהְיוֹת תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: If the Ninth of Av happened to fall on Shabbat eve
they bring him an egg-bulk and he eats
so that he should not enter Shabbat
while he is afflicted (fasting)

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from שבת coming before the fast to the fast coming right before שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When תשעה באב is on ערב שבת, one eats a כביצה before שבת so as not to enter שבת while fasting.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא ate an egg to teach the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: ר' יהודה reports that ר' עקיבא, on a תשעה באב that fell on ערב שבת, swallowed a lightly cooked egg without salt. He did it to show his students the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: ר' יהודה said, we were once sitting before ר' עקיבא on a תשעה באב that fell on ערב שבת. They brought him a lightly cooked egg, and he swallowed it without salt. He did this not because he craved it, but to show the students the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story, a מעשה, that backs up the rule from the previous step. It shows a great teacher actually practicing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail of the story makes a point. ר' עקיבא ate only a small egg, with no salt, and without enjoyment. This shows that eating before שבת is a minimal act done for the sake of the הלכה, not a real meal. A מעשה רב (an act by a great sage) is strong proof of how the law is practiced.

keyTerms.meaning: To demonstrate the law in practice

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִינוּ יוֹשְׁבִין לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Once we were sitting before Rabbi Akiva

phrases.aramaic: וְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיָה.
phrases.english: and it was the Ninth of Av that fell on Shabbat eve
and they brought him a lightly cooked egg
and he swallowed it without salt
and not because he craved it
but rather to show the students the halakha

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיִינוּ יוֹשְׁבִין לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of eating a כביצה on a תשעה באב that falls on ערב שבת with a story about ר' עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one does not complete the fast when תשעה באב is on ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A מעשה with ר' עקיבא, reported by ר' יהודה, who ate an egg in front of his students on such a day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: one must complete the fast
steps.stepSummary: ר' יוסי disagrees and rules that one fasts and completes the fast even when תשעה באב is on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ר' יוסי says: he fasts and completes the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is introduced. ר' יוסי argues with the first view and with ר' עקיבא's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ר' יוסי, finishing the fast comes first, even if that means entering שבת while still fasting. This sets up a מחלוקת, and the next steps show each side's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He fasts and completes the fast (until nightfall)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says
he fasts and completes the fast

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מִתְעַנֶּה וּמַשְׁלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to the ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ר' יוסי, one completes the fast of תשעה באב even when it falls on ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks whether they agree about תשעה באב on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: ר' יוסי asks the חכמים whether they agree that when תשעה באב is on Sunday, one stops eating on שבת while it is still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: ר' יוסי said to them: Don't you agree with me that when תשעה באב falls on Sunday, a person stops eating while it is still daytime on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: ר' יוסי begins building his argument. First he asks a question to get his opponents to agree to a case. He will use that case against them in the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the fast begins Saturday night, the fast must start before dark, while it is still שבת. So a person spends the last part of שבת not eating. ר' יוסי wants the חכמים to admit this so he can compare it to his own case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the week, Sunday

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them
Do you not agree with me

phrases.aramaic: בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶחָד בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: regarding the Ninth of Av that falls on Sunday
that he stops eating while it is still day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ר' יוסי begins defending his opinion by asking about a case his opponents already accept.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים agree that when תשעה באב is on Sunday, one stops eating before שבת ends.

steps.title: The חכמים agree
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer, 'Yes,' and agree to ר' יוסי's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes, indeed.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים confirm the case ר' יוסי asked about. This gives him the shared starting point he needs for his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אֲבָל' here means 'yes, indeed' and not 'but.' Now both sides agree that a person can spend the end of שבת fasting.
steps.confusionAlert: In Modern Hebrew, אֲבָל means 'but.' Here it is an old word of agreement meaning 'yes, certainly.'

phrases.english: They said to him: Indeed (yes)

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֲבָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ר' יוסי's question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the חכמים agree that one stops eating on שבת afternoon before a Sunday תשעה באב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: entering or leaving שבת afflicted is the same
steps.stepSummary: ר' יוסי argues that if leaving שבת while fasting is acceptable, entering שבת while fasting should be acceptable too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What difference is there to me between entering שבת while fasting and leaving שבת while fasting?
steps.whatsHappening: ר' יוסי now uses the agreed case to challenge the חכמים. He claims his case and theirs are really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, part of שבת is spent in עינוי. If the חכמים allow it at the end of שבת, ר' יוסי asks why it should be forbidden at the start of שבת. If his comparison works, then one should finish the fast on ערב שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to me? (there is no difference)

phrases.english: He said to them

phrases.aramaic: מַה לִּי לִיכָּנֵס בָּהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא מְעוּנֶּה,
phrases.english: What difference to me is entering it while afflicted

phrases.aramaic: מַה לִּי לָצֵאת מִמֶּנָּה כְּשֶׁהוּא מְעוּנֶּה.
phrases.english: and what difference to me is leaving it while afflicted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה לִּי לִיכָּנֵס בָּהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא מְעוּנֶּה, מַה לִּי לָצֵאת מִמֶּנָּה כְּשֶׁהוּא מְעוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the agreement from step 6 to attack the חכמים' position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' rule (step 2) that one must not enter שבת while fasting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים already allow being afflicted at the end of שבת. Being afflicted at the start of שבת is no different, so their rule has no basis.

steps.title: The חכמים: leaving after a full day of eating is different
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the comparison. A person leaving שבת has eaten all day, while a person entering שבת has not eaten all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If you speak about leaving שבת while fasting, that is because he ate and drank the whole day. Would you say the same about entering שבת while fasting, when he has not eaten or drunk the whole day?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer ר' יוסי by showing that his two cases are not equal. This defends their original ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of שבת, a person has been eating all day, so a short fast before dark causes no real suffering. Before שבת on תשעה באב, a person has fasted all day, so starting שבת hungry is real עינוי. The difference in how afflicted the person actually is breaks ר' יוסי's comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: If you said (opens a 'this case is different' rebuttal)
Will you say? (questions whether the same applies)

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת: the חכמים (and ר' עקיבא's practice) hold that when תשעה באב is on ערב שבת, one eats a כביצה so as not to enter שבת fasting. ר' יוסי holds one completes the fast. ר' יוסי compares this to stopping before a Sunday fast. The חכמים answer that leaving שבת after eating all day is not real suffering, but entering שבת after fasting all day is.

phrases.english: They said to him
If you said that about leaving it

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָכַל וְשָׁתָה כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: that is because he ate and drank the entire day
will you say the same about entering it while afflicted

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא אָכַל וְשָׁתָה כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: when he has not eaten or drunk the entire day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם אָמַרְתָּ לָצֵאת מִמֶּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ר' יוסי's comparison in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between leaving שבת while fasting and entering שבת while fasting.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ in real suffering. One who leaves שבת has eaten all day, while one who enters שבת has fasted all day.

steps.title: עולא rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: a fast on ערב שבת is completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: After the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the חכמים, עולא tells us whose opinion we follow in practice. He picks רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 to 8 laid out a debate about finishing a fast on ערב שבת. עולא now gives the practical ruling: when תשעה באב is on Friday, you fast all the way into שבת. The rest of this passage will test whether this ruling holds up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the target of every challenge that follows next.

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the debate from steps 4 to 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי. A fast on ערב שבת (such as תשעה באב) is completed.

steps.title: A source showing רבן גמליאל did not complete the fast on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether we really follow רבי יוסי. It cites a source where רבי מאיר says רבן גמליאל agreed that a fast on ערב שבת is not completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really act like רבי יוסי? A contradiction is raised from a source. We do not decree a public fast on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים. But if a series of fasts already began, it is not stopped; these are the words of רבן גמליאל. רבי מאיר said: Even though רבן גמליאל said they do not stop, he agreed that they do not complete the fast. The same applies to תשעה באב that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's ruling. It brings a source showing that רבן גמליאל held that a fast on ערב שבת is not completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל says that a series of fasts that already started continues even on festive days. However, רבי מאיר reports that he agreed you stop before the end of the day. רבי מאיר applies the same rule to תשעה באב on Friday. This directly contradicts רבי יוסי's view that you fast all day.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it: introduces a source that contradicts what was just said
Stopping or interrupting a series of fasts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'אין מפסיקין' with 'אין משלימין'. 'אין מפסיקין' means the fast day is still kept. 'אין משלימין' means you do not fast until night. רבן גמליאל holds both at once: you fast, but you stop early.

phrases.english: But do we really act like Rabbi Yosei?
And they raised a contradiction:
We do not decree a fast upon the public
on Rosh Chodesh, Chanukah, or Purim.
And if they already began, they do not interrupt,
phrases.notes: If a series of fasts was already underway, a day in the series that lands on these dates is still kept.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.
Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵין מַפְסִיקִין,
phrases.english: Even though Rabban Gamliel said they do not interrupt,
he agreed that they do not complete the fast,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and so too with the Ninth of Av that falls on Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל, as reported by רבי מאיר, holds that a fast on ערב שבת is not completed. This is the opposite of רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: The הלכה was firmly fixed like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבן גמליאל's rulings on fasts were accepted as binding. Even רבי יהושע could not overturn them after רבן גמליאל died.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: After רבן גמליאל passed away, רבי יהושע came to cancel his rulings. רבי יוחנן בן נורי stood up and said: I see that the body follows the head. All of רבן גמליאל's life we set the הלכה like him, and now you want to cancel his words? יהושע, we do not listen to you. The הלכה was already set like רבן גמליאל, and no one ever disputed it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with a story. The story shows that רבן גמליאל's ruling about fasts became the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 only showed what רבן גמליאל held. This ברייתא adds that his view was the fixed, accepted practice that no one challenged. That makes the challenge to עולא much stronger, since the accepted הלכה seems to be against רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The body follows the head: we follow the leader's established rulings

phrases.english: And it was taught:
After the passing of Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנַס רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְהָפֵר אֶת דְּבָרָיו.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua entered to annul his words.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood on his feet and said:

phrases.aramaic: חָזֵי אֲנָא דְּבָתַר רֵישָׁא גּוּפָא אָזֵיל.
phrases.english: I see that the body follows the head.
All the days of Rabban Gamliel
we established the halakha like him,
and now you seek to cancel his words?!
Yehoshua, we do not listen to you,
for the halakha was already established like Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁעִרְעֵר בַּדָּבָר כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: and there was no one who disputed the matter at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: לְאַחַר פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 10 by showing that רבן גמליאל's view was the accepted הלכה.
steps.raayaObject: That the accepted הלכה is like רבן גמליאל, so a fast on ערב שבת is not completed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי יוחנן בן נורי blocking רבי יהושע from overturning רבן גמליאל's rulings.

steps.title: Each generation followed its own leader
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל's generation followed him, but רבי יוסי's later generation followed רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the generation of רבן גמליאל, they acted like רבן גמליאל. In the generation of רבי יוסי, they acted like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. The story of step 11 describes an earlier time; later, the practice moved to רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that רבן גמליאל's ruling was once fixed. It limits that ruling to his own era. From רבי יוסי's generation on, the practice followed רבי יוסי, so עולא's ruling stands.

phrases.aramaic: בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עֲבוּד כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: In the generation of Rabban Gamliel they acted like Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי עֲבוּד כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: in the generation of Rabbi Yosei they acted like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עֲבוּד כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10 and 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a particular time period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the הלכה was fixed like רבן גמליאל, it must still follow him, against רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל's ruling governed only his own generation. Later generations followed רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Questioning whether רבן גמליאל's generation really followed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבן גמליאל's own generation followed him. It cites רבי אלעזר בן צדוק's family story about a postponed תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really act like רבן גמליאל in his own generation? Was it not taught that רבי אלעזר בן צדוק said: I am from the descendants of סנאב בן בנימין. Once, תשעה באב fell on שבת, and we pushed it off until after שבת. We fasted on it but did not complete it, because that day was our family's יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer of step 12. It brings a story from someone who lived in רבן גמליאל's time to check how people actually behaved then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק's family celebrated a family festival on the tenth of אב. When the fast was moved to Sunday, the tenth, they fasted but stopped early. Notice the reason given: the day itself was their יום טוב. The next step draws the key inference from this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancestral family that brought wood for the מזבח on the tenth of אב and kept that day as a family festival

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עֲבוּד כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: And in the generation of Rabban Gamliel did they act like Rabban Gamliel?
But was it not taught:
Rabbi Elazar (ben) Tzadok said:
I (was) of the descendants of Sena'av ben Binyamin.

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת חָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Once the Ninth of Av fell on Shabbat,
and we postponed it until after Shabbat,
and we fasted on it, but did not complete it,
because it was our Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עֲבוּד כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that רבן גמליאל's generation acted like רבן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contemporary of רבן גמליאל explains that his family stopped the fast early only because the day itself was a festival. This suggests that otherwise they would have completed it.

steps.title: Inference: on the eve of a festival, they completed the fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that they stopped early only because the day itself was a יום טוב. On ערב יום טוב, they would have completed the fast, which matches רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason was that it was a יום טוב. This implies that on ערב יום טוב, they complete the fast!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the punchline from רבי אלעזר בן צדוק's story. Even in רבן גמליאל's generation, a fast on the eve of a festival was completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being the eve of a festival were enough to stop early, the family would not have needed the stronger reason that the day itself was a festival. So the eve of a festival does not cut the fast short. This contradicts the claim that רבן גמליאל's generation followed his view.

keyTerms.meaning: But this implies: introduces an inference from the opposite case

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not in what the story says outright, but in what it implies. The family gave 'it was our יום טוב' as the reason. That reason only makes sense if the eve of a festival alone would not have stopped the fast.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: even in רבן גמליאל's own era, people seem to have completed fasts on the eve of a festival, as רבי יוסי holds. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: The reason is because it was a Festival,
but on the eve of a Festival, they complete it!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּיוֹם טוֹב, הָא עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב מַשְׁלִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference that completes the challenge begun in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That even in רבן גמליאל's generation, a fast on the eve of a festival was completed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The stated reason in רבי אלעזר בן צדוק's ברייתא: they stopped early because the day itself was their יום טוב.

steps.title: A rabbinic festival is different from שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the proof from the family story. Their festival was only rabbinic, so its rules do not carry over to ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: A rabbinic festival is different. Since one may fast on it for some hours, one completes a fast on its eve until nightfall. But on שבת one may not fast even for a few hours, so one does not complete a fast on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on the proof from step 14. He says that story tells us nothing about ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא reasoned that on ערב יום טוב the family would have finished the fast, which matches רבי יוסי. רבינא answers that their festival was only a rabbinic יום טוב, and partial fasting is allowed on such a day. שבת is stricter because no fasting at all is allowed on it, so a fast on ערב שבת is not completed. The proof does not reach שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival made by the Rabbis, not from the Torah
Fasting for part of the day (some hours)
Until evening, meaning finishing the fast fully

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'מַשְׁלִימִין בּוֹ' do not mean finishing a fast on the festival itself. They mean finishing a fast that falls on the day before it.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
A rabbinic festival is different,
since one may fast on it for some hours,
one completes [a fast on its eve] until evening.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a fast that falls on the day before a rabbinic festival.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת, הוֹאִיל וְאֵין מִתְעַנִּין בָּהּ שָׁעוֹת
phrases.english: Shabbat, since one may not fast on it even for some hours,
one does not complete [a fast on its eve] until evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל דִּבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 13–14, defending step 12's claim that רבן גמליאל's generation followed him.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the family story, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compared a rabbinic festival to שבת. But a rabbinic festival is more lenient, because partial fasting is allowed on it.

steps.title: רב יוסף does not remember the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he never heard the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I did not hear this ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says he does not know the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had become ill and forgotten his learning. His claim that he never heard the ruling opens the door for his student to show him the source.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I did not hear this ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over proofs to the question of where the ruling for רבי יוסי comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recognize the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף of the source
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught this ruling. He taught it on the משנה about public fasts, where the חכמים say one fasts and completes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it to us on this: 'We do not decree a public fast on ראש חודש, etc.' On that we said: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר, who said it in the name of רבן גמליאל. But the חכמים say: one fasts and completes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows רב יוסף that the ruling came from his own teaching. It is based on a statement of the חכמים that one completes the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה includes רבי מאיר's report that a fast on ערב שבת is not completed. רב, quoted by רב יהודה, said this is only the view of רבי מאיר in the name of רבן גמליאל. The חכמים disagree and say one fasts and completes, which matches רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: One fasts and completes the fast

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You told it to us,
and it was on this that you told it to us:
We do not decree a fast upon the public
on New Moons, etc.,
phrases.notes: The full משנה also mentions חנוכה, פורים, and רבי מאיר's report about ערב שבת.

phrases.english: and we said about it,
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir
which he said in the name of Rabban Gamliel,
but the Rabbis say:
One fasts and completes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן וְאַהָא אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim that he never heard the ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a fast on ערב שבת is completed, as רבי יוסי holds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב on the משנה: 'the חכמים say: one fasts and completes.'

steps.title: Does the חכמים' view cover every case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the חכמים's 'one completes' applies to all the cases in the משנה, including ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this refer to all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how אביי's source would prove the ruling. It assumes the חכמים disagree with every case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the חכמים's ruling also covers the case of a fast on ערב שבת. So the גמרא asks whether their words apply to all the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested proof)

phrases.english: What, is it not [said] about all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו אַכּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the assumption that אביי's proof depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים rule a fast on ערב שבת is completed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading 'מִתְעַנֶּה וּמַשְׁלִים' as applying to every case in the משנה.

steps.title: Only חנוכה and פורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. The חכמים's ruling may refer only to חנוכה and פורים, not to ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to חנוכה and פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers no. The חכמים may have been speaking only about fasts on חנוכה and פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים only argue about חנוכה and פורים, then they might agree that a fast on ערב שבת is not completed. That would mean the source does not prove the ruling for רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not deny the ruling for רבי יוסי. It only shows that this particular source may not prove it.

phrases.english: No, [it refers] to Hanukkah and Purim.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אַחֲנוּכָּה וּפוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the broad reading suggested in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the חכמים's ruling to חנוכה and פורים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ruling covers all the cases. But it may cover only the rabbinic festivals.

steps.title: This reading is also logical
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to support the narrow reading with a logical argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is reasonable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to show why limiting the חכמים to חנוכה and פורים makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא' tells us that support for the answer in step 19 is coming. The actual reasoning continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces support for the answer given in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים's ruling refers only to חנוכה and פורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical argument that continues on the next amud.
